messages:
Maya (Support): FYI incoming escalation from a customer — streaming requests intermittently end with 'broken pipe' and our gateway is marking them as 5xx. Customer says this bumps their billing and triggers alerts. Repro attached.

Maya (Support): Repro steps:
1) curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-stream-1","input":"stream me plz"}' https://api.redwood.inference/v1/stream
2) After ~5-12s client closes socket (simulate network flake)
Expected: server should classify as client_abort / user disconnect (not 5xx). Actual: we log 502 gateway_error and increment 5xx counter.

Maya (Support): Logs from customer's trace (sanitized):
```
proxy: upstream write: broken pipe (errno=32)
gateway: connection closed by peer, status_code=0
metering: counted_response=502
```

Eli (Runtime Eng): Thanks, filing to runtime team. Can you paste the full gateway request-id and sample x-forwarded-for? Also which client lib? Node fetch or curl? Did they use chunked encoding explicitly?

Maya (Support): request-id: req_01H8YZXYZ; client: node-fetch v3 (AWS Lambda). They send Transfer-Encoding: chunked and stream body. Customer also included tcpdump showing FIN from client after server sent some chunks.

Jason (SRE): This smells like our proxied connection close heuristic. If upstream sends EOF before headers complete, we mark 5xx. But if client closed first we should mark user_abort. Can we get the proxy logs for req_01H8YZXYZ? @Eli can you check gateway logs for connection states around that id?

Eli (Runtime Eng): grabbing logs now — saw pattern: backend returned partial chunked payload, then client FIN arrives. Our gateway sees backend write error (EPIPE) and treats as upstream failure. We need to distinguish EPIPE caused by client vs backend.

Eli (Runtime Eng): Quick repro I ran locally:
```
# server: python simple chunked responder
python -c "import time,sys; sys.stdout.write('HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n'); sys.stdout.write('5\r\nhello\r\n'); sys.stdout.flush(); time.sleep(2); sys.stdout.write('0\r\n\r\n'); sys.stdout.flush()"
# client: curl -N, then kill -9 after first chunk
```
Gateway logs:
```
[gateway] write to client: EPIPE
[ingest] classify_response: status=502
```

Priya (Billing): If these are being counted as 5xx they're affecting customer monthly invoices? We had a complaint. Can we add a filter to exclude 'client_abort' from billable 5xx until fix shipped?

Jason (SRE): We'll need to be careful to not undercount real upstream errors. Suggest adding a temporary metric filter: if request-duration < 30s and gateway_write_error contains 'EPIPE' and tcp_state shows client closed -> tag as user_abort and exclude from billing aggregate for now.

Support Bot: New ticket created: TKT-2026-733 | escalation | streaming-broken-pipe -> assigned to Eli, Jason

Maya (Support): Customer is ok with workaround if we can update billing and backfill for last week. They provided list of request ids.

Eli (Runtime Eng): Plan:
- short-term: add heuristic to gateway to check if client FIN arrived before backend error and label as client_abort (PR target: next 24h)
- medium: update classification doc and add unit tests for chunked flows
- longer: add connection state tracing and a dashboard for 'client-abort vs upstream-fail'

Jason (SRE): I'll implement the metric filter and a temporary analytics query to compute potential refunds. Priya will review.

Priya (Billing): I'll start compiling impacted invoices and scope refunds once we confirm. Also we need a KB entry on 'streaming client disconnects' for support.

Maya (Support): Thanks. Assigning follow-ups:
- @Eli: PR for heuristic (due EOD)
- @Jason: metric filter + analytics query (due EOD)
- @Priya: compile invoice list & hold refunds until confirm (due tomorrow)
- @Maya: send customer interim update

Eli (Runtime Eng): pushing PR now -> https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/5243 : adds check for client FIN in connection state before counting gateway EPIPE as upstream error. Includes unit test harness. cc @Jason

Jason (SRE): deployed metric filter to staging; results show ~120 events in last 7 days that match heuristic. Sending raw ids to Priya.

Priya (Billing): got the list, thanks. Opening proposal for credits.

Maya (Support): Customer updated: appreciate the quick attention; will await confirmation. :relieved:

Eli (Runtime Eng): Merged PR, rolling to canary now. If canary looks good we'll roll to prod tonight. Watching metrics.

Support Bot: Deployment notice: canary rollout started for runtime gateway PR 5243

Eli (Runtime Eng): Canary looks clean for 30m, no regression in true upstream 5xx. Marking for prod roll.

Jason (SRE): Prod roll started. Adding alert to watch for spike in 5xx-> user_abort flip.

Maya (Support): Customer notified of upcoming fix and potential credits. They'll follow up if anything else.

Priya (Billing): Will prepare credit memos; hold until we confirm numbers post-rollout.

Maya (Support): Closing thread when credits are finalized and tickets resolved. Thanks team :raised_hands:
